Planet & station map

Top 20 alliances by military score, growth rates over the last ~5.1 days of dump history (window shown per snapshot). Click a column header to sort. Facts only; verify anything time-critical in game.

Every player with colonized planets — every alliance's members included — sorted by distance from your home system once you set it below (Euclidean, system coordinates, measured to the target's nearest planet; the Nearest system column names that system, so you can read your raid range at a glance). Your home system is saved in this browser only — nothing is uploaded. Chips: INACTIVE Nd = zero delta on economy and overall score for N consecutive daily snapshots; VACATION = flagged vacation mode; NO ALLIANCE = active player with no alliance tag; NEW Nd = homeworld colonized ≤14 days ago (join date proxied by homeworld colonization — the dumps carry no explicit signup date). "New players only" + "no alliance only" together = recruit-scout mode: fresh unallianced players near your space. The search box narrows any view by typed text — matches player name, alliance tag, any of their systems ("A3-12"), or their sector (short code "A3" or full "Alpha Arm - Sector 3") — and combines with the checkboxes. Click any column header to sort. Snapshot 2026-08-29 10:59 UTC.

Caveats: vacation players cannot be attacked (tracked for awareness). Player-reported but unverified: inactive players stop producing ~24h after being flagged — treat loot expectations accordingly. Activity is inferred from daily score snapshots (a player can be active without scoring in a given window).

Every station across all six arms. Owner column shows the holding alliance's tag (or "neutral"). Capture column counts down live from the snapshotted captureEndsAt timestamp. Building levels are packed: Dock · Shield · Turret · Storage. Basics = ore + silicates + hydrogen + alloys. Click a column header to sort. Facts only, snapshot 2026-08-29 10:59 UTC.

Station rework quick-reference and battle planner. Each side fields at most 8,000 CP of ships; fleets are never split (a fleet either fits whole or goes to Reserve); the station's docked garrison consumes defender CP first; one decisive battle after a 45-min prep; no retreat; attacker must win outright.

Command point reference

CP cost per ship, sorted cheap first. 8,000 CP cap per side per battle; fleets are never split; the docked garrison consumes defender CP first, so junk left docked crowds reinforcing fleets out of the budget. Greyed rows are unreleased (from the patch-notes leak).

Fleet CP calculator

Enter counts to see live CP against the 8,000 cap. Efficiency shown at vanilla tech — with tech applied, atk/CP scales with your weapon bonuses.

Fleet comps — quick reference 2026-07-27 rev 3

The best 8,000-CP fleet compositions from the full-catalog sim study (44 compositions, every one tested against every other, on this page's engine; all numbers at zero tech; a drawn battle means the defender keeps the station). EW ships: not worth fielding — the jamming strength is published nowhere, and at every strength tested the ships they replace are worth more. Station battle simulator

Runs the real battle engine in your browser. Fill in the composition and tech bonuses on each side. Station shield & turrets are an APPROXIMATION — the engine models fleets, so I model the station as a big-hull "shield" ship and the turret building Lv N as N turret units (attack ~475 each — decoded from a real station battle report; hull 1,000 each — from dump turretMaxHp = 1,000 × level; kinetic). Treat results as directional, not a promise. A draw is a defender hold under the new capture rules. Carrier wings: set each side's wing assignment and Carrier Ops level below its commander. Each carrier buffs 16 + level fighters (17 at L1 → 21 at L5; +25% ATK / 15% dodge) or bombers (+30% HP); Auto wings fighters first, leftover carriers wing bombers. Fighter counts are confirmed from the in-game carrier card; the bomber count (4 + level → 5–9) is an unverified read of the same "+1 slot/level" card — no bomber wing on hand to check. Winging is CP-neutral, so the CP stamps don't change.

Transcribed 2026-07-20 from the player-made "Nexus Legacy Cheat Sheet" by xClaw (contributors: Jimbobicus — tech tree, Uetri — mining calculator), shared on the official Discord. Player-tested field results, not verified formulas — if the sheet updates or the game rebalances, this page lags until re-transcribed. Techs column = the submitting player's own techs (clarified 2026-07-13; different submitters explain the varying values) — sim checks stay vanilla both sides, so they're slightly conservative vs a teched player.

Sim check: every row with a recorded enemy composition was replayed on the calibrated battle engine at vanilla tech both sides (ranges checked at both ends). ✓ = engine reproduces the sheet's result · ~ = agrees at the low end of the range but bleeds/fails at the top end · ✗ = engine disagrees · n/a = no enemy comp to sim against. Verdict across the sheet: the data holds up — 15 of 16 dead-space mining rows and all pirate-camp rows reproduce exactly (latest: the 40-MV / 50-BS / 293-MC row added 2026-07-20, sim-confirmed).

Sim verdict on the dead-space table: 15 of 16 simmable rows reproduce exactly at vanilla tech (held rows sim at 99–100% hold, wiped rows at 0%); the 'draw' row sims as a hold with ~21 losses. The sheet and the calibrated engine corroborate each other.

Pirate raid size appears to scale with the mining fleet — the 105-vessel run drew a 1,254-ship raid and was wiped despite a 100-cruiser escort.

Sim suggestion for the 'draw' row: the sheet's BS core is right — an equal-size cruiser wall gets wiped by this raid in-model, and adding fighter chaff makes it WORSE (the raid's 59 Cruisers rapid-fire fighters ×4). Adding ~60 Cruisers to the BS core trims expected escort losses from ~21 to ~15; otherwise fly it as-is and budget ~20 escort losses.

EW Ships appear in most successful large runs; the engine models them as plain hulls (jamming not modeled), so their real contribution is likely understated here.

Sim verdicts (vanilla, both ends of each range): 21–25 Intys → 100% win, 0–2 losses (matches 'occasional Inty loss' exactly). 7 Cruisers → 100% / 0 losses at both ends — also matches our own independent solver from 2026-07-03. 60 Cruisers → clean at the low end but 89% / 36 losses vs a max-roll encounter. 25 Cru + 25 MC → clean at the low end but 7% win vs max roll (missile cruisers have no scout/fighter rapid-fire). The sheet's own 'highly depends on your military techs and Warlord' hedge is consistent with the top-end bleed.

The '1 Scout' small-anomaly row is not reproducible as a combat fleet (instant loss in-engine) — it likely refers to the no-pirates sentinel anomaly case (hazard only), matching Determinor's guide.

Zone labels are OUR inference — the sheet's three column groups carry no zone names. Grounds: the middle group's encounter range matches Determinor's published Open-anomaly roll (5–20 Scouts + 2–10 Fighters, hard variants add Intys) almost exactly; battleship-bearing spawns match the dead-space raid pool seen in the mining table; the trivial left group matches sentinel-zone content.

Rolling change log, newest day first. Diffed each publish against the previous snapshot; the full 14-day window is shown (5,798 events in this snapshot). Facts only. Diff snapshot 2026-08-29 10:59 UTC.

Enter the enemy fleet (from a spy report), then either check the fleet you already have — direct verdict with expected losses on both sides and the replacement bill for your losses — or tick the hulls you can build and search counter-compositions from scratch. When your fleet falls short, the advisor searches the smallest reinforcements that turn it into a pass: additions drawn from your buildable hulls (including hulls you don't own yet — e.g. battleships you can build but haven't), stacked on top of what you have, plus plain "more of your current mix". The battle engine runs in your browser; resource bills are exact build-screen numbers, no market conversion. Recommendations are the margined size, not the knife-edge minimum: sim counts are estimates (see Method), the default adds +25%. Vanilla tech both sides. Carrier wings (card-confirmed; the game makes you assign each carrier's wing before launch): each carrier buffs 16 + Carrier Ops level fighters (17→21; +25% ATK / 15% dodge) OR bombers (+30% HP) OR shuttles (no combat buff). Set Your carrier wings and Your Carrier Ops level to match your account; enemy carriers are always assumed worst-case (fighters first, leftovers wing bombers, Ops L5). Fighter scaling is confirmed in-game; the bomber count (4 + level → 5–9) is unverified. Fleet entries persist in your browser between visits.

Where these numbers come from

Counter matrix: ~950 simulation batteries on the community battle engine (nexuslegacytools). Every stat visible on in-game ship cards matches the engine exactly, and shield pools are server-confirmed (shipyard API, 2026-07-18) — the engine's HP/shield/attack numbers are exact game data. No weapon-vs-armor multipliers exist in the game (battle-report-fitted calibration + client audit, settled 2026-07-18); armor class is taxonomy for the rapid-fire tables. EW jamming is real but unmodeled — its formula is not publicly known. Round cap, damage variance, and shield regen use the fan site's calibration fitted against 595 logged real battles (constants: 15 rounds, variance 0, regen 0.4; refreshed each publish). Fit quality is rough (mean error ~0.5) — trust composition choices over exact counts. Pure-type duels at vanilla tech; mixed fleets shift rapid-fire economics substantially. The matrix's Carrier row is bare hulls — the card-confirmed fighter wing buff (16 + Carrier Ops level) is a mixed-fleet composition, so it lives in the Fleet Advisor and Battle Sim (which model it, with a per-side Carrier Ops selector), not in a pure-type table. Bomber ×3 vs defense buildings also not shown (the engine sims fleet-vs-fleet only).

Targets / Stations / Sectors / Ticker: joined nightly from the fan site's per-arm universe dumps + player score histories. INACTIVE = consecutive daily snapshots with zero economy and overall score delta (a player can be active without scoring); VACATION comes straight from the dump and such players cannot be attacked. The claim that inactive players stop producing ~24h after being flagged is player-reported and unverified. Station stocks, shields, and capture timers are as-of the snapshot stamp; the Ticker is a day-over-day diff of consecutive snapshots, so same-day events can land a day late. Sector-control fields exist in the dump but are not yet populated by the game.

Combat: loss events are military-score drops between consecutive history points. The history arrives in polling waves (~5/day), so a "when" is really a ~4–6 hour window and co-timing between players means nothing. No attacker/defender attribution is possible from scores; winners often lose ~nothing so battles read one-sided; PvE losses included. Waves where ≥15% of all players drop at once are treated as score recalcs and excluded. Hot systems map losses to the LOSING player's home systems — right for defenders, wrong for attackers who died elsewhere.

PvE Fleets: static hand-transcription of the community "Nexus Legacy Cheat Sheet" (xClaw + contributors, shared on the official Discord) — player-tested results, NOT auto-updating and NOT verified formulas; re-transcribe when the sheet changes. Every row carrying an enemy composition is sim-checked on the calibrated engine at vanilla tech (see the chips on that tab); the mining and pirate-camp tables reproduce almost exactly, which cross-validates both the sheet and the engine.

Intel: joined from nexuslegacytools public JSON dumps (players, alliances, per-arm universe data, 7-day histories). Score/ranking snapshots only — no private account data exists in the dumps. The station/planet feed lags live play. The intel browser covers the top 50 alliances by military score.

Fleet advisor: runs the same battle engine in your browser. Check my fleet sims your entered fleet directly (600 runs); on a shortfall it binary-searches the smallest reinforcement that passes — each doctrine composition from your buildable hulls added on top of your existing fleet, plus "more of your current mix" — so the suggestion can include hulls you can build but don't own yet. Find counters binary-searches each composition from scratch. Both add your safety margin and price results with exact per-resource build bills (no market conversion) — bills load automatically from every captured cost screen, so a new screenshot upgrades the advisor with no code change. Carrier wings are card-confirmed and pre-assigned in game (each carrier buffs fighters OR bombers OR shuttles — one role, chosen before launch). Hangar capacity scales with Carrier Operations research: 16 + level fighters per carrier (17→21; +25% ATK, dodge approximated as bonus EHP) or 4 + level bombers (5→9; +30% HP, applied to hull — this bomber number is unverified, no bomber wing checked). The Your carrier wings and Your Carrier Ops level selectors tell the sim what YOUR carriers fly; enemy carriers are always assumed worst-case (fighters first, leftover carriers wing bombers, Ops L5). Fleet entries and hull ticks persist in your browser (localStorage, this device only). Same model caveats as the matrix: trust the composition choice more than the exact count; the margin exists because the counts are estimates.

Wanted for calibration: shipyard cost screens for Torpedo Frigate / Battleship / Bomber (Carrier landed 2026-07-13), and ANY battle report with 100+ ships per side. Those two things upgrade every number on this page.
